answer: The help center shows two forms retired in 2026, both on February 1, 2026. The notarized power of attorney NW-POA-1 was replaced by NW-POA-2, which can be signed electronically with no notary. In Georgia, though, a power of attorney including NW-POA-2 still has to be notarized. An NW-POA-1 signed before February 1, 2026 was accepted until June 30, 2026, so it is no longer accepted as of today. The odometer disclosure statement NW-ODO-1 was replaced by NW-ODO-2. Note that the older article "Broken or replaced odometer" (from 2022) still names NW-ODO-1, so for the 'not actual mileage' case use NW-ODO-2. If you need a complete official list of retired forms, the help center may not have it, so check with a store.
